problem: VLN agents rely on pre-trained visual backbones (ResNet/CLIP) that are sensitive to viewpoint change and fail to recognize the same object across views. Zero-shot LLM/VLM agents lack VLN domain knowledge, while fine-tuning LLMs/VLMs is computationally expensive.
motivation: Agent actions only change viewpoint, not the environment, so an ideal agent should recognize the same objects across observations. Contrastive learning can extract shared information between observations, but randomly chosen history frames do not necessarily share content, so a weak signal from a VLM is used to pick positives without fine-tuning the VLM.
key_idea: Use a frozen VLM (LLaVA-1.5) to list objects per observation, build a binary sample-selection matrix from object overlap, and apply InfoNCE only on a partial slice of the visual feature (partial contrastive learning) inside a DUET agent.
insight: The VLM only supplies a weak, cheap positive/negative selection signal, so the agent inherits VLM object knowledge without VLM biases or fine-tuning cost. Contrastive loss is applied only to a fraction (lambda=0.2) of the feature dimensions, leaving the rest free for viewpoint, noise and unshared objects. Ablations show the choice of VLM (LLaVA 1.5/1.6, OpenFlamingo, BLIP-2) barely changes SR, and the prompt must exclude ubiquitous objects (walls, floors) or all frames become positives.
method: VLM object extraction: LLaVA v1.5 prompted to list objects (ignoring walls/floors/rooftops, comma-separated) for each observation in the history
Sample selection matrix A: N×N symmetric binary matrix, A_ij=1 iff the two observations share at least m objects (m=1)
Positive/negative sampling: pairs with A_ij=1 are positives; a frame k is a negative for a pair if A_ik=0 and A_jk=0
Partial contrastive module: a single-layer FFN on CLIP ViT-B/16 features outputs h=[h_objs; h_flex]; InfoNCE (cosine, temperature tau) applied only on h_objs (lambda=0.2 of dims)
DUET action prediction: dual-scale graph transformer with global topological map and local branch, dynamic fusion
Overall loss: gamma*L_SAP + L_PID + L_OG + alpha*L_pcon (gamma=1, alpha=0.5); LXMERT init, 100k pre-train iterations at batch 32, 20k fine-tune iterations at batch 8

setting.backbone: DUET (LXMERT-initialized, trained) + CLIP ViT-B/16 visual features + frozen LLaVA-1.5 as weak supervisor (training only)
setting.training_data: R2R / REVERIE / SOON training sets with standard DUET pipeline (SAP, OG, pseudo interactive demonstrator); no extra data, no VLM fine-tuning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB observations (CLIP features) with observation history/topological map
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (DUET global/local action prediction)
setting.privileged: none at test time (VLM only used to produce training-time supervision)

numbers.backbone: DUET + CLIP ViT-B/16, LLaVA-1.5 weak supervision

numbers_note: VLM-choice sensitivity is given only in a figure (SR), with no numeric values.
results: On R2R val-unseen WPCL reaches SR 78 / SPL 70 / NE 2.69, beating DUET (72/60), GOAT (77/68), GridMM (75/64) and BEVBert (75/64), and far above zero-shot LLM agents (NavGPT 34, DiscussNav 43). On REVERIE val-unseen it reaches SR 54.03 / SPL 37.41 (vs GOAT 53.37/36.70), and on SOON val-unseen SR 42.92 / SPL 26.57 (vs GOAT 40.50/25.18). It trains on a single 24GB GPU.
limitations: No ablations on lambda, m or the partial vs full contrastive loss are reported, and VLM object detection accuracy is not measured because object labels are absent
Gains over the strongest non-LLM baseline (GOAT) are small on several metrics (e.g. R2R val-seen SR 82 vs 83, REVERIE val-seen SPL 71.39 vs 71.40)
Only object-overlap binary signals are used; the VLM still runs on every history frame during training, and only simulator, discrete-graph benchmarks are evaluated
